title: CTAB Chloroform DNA Extraction from Ethanol-Preserved Filters
author: Dominique L. Chaput
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bw8gphtw

steps.title: Preserve samples in ethanol
steps.instruction: Place each 47 mm polycarbonate filter (0.2 µm or 0.4 µm) that collected 50–200 mL pond water, or 25–50 mg of sediment/soil/faeces/tissue (5–10 mg for inhibitor‑rich samples), into a 2 mL screw‑cap cryotube containing 100 % molecular‑grade ethanol; store tubes at –20 °C until arrival at the laboratory.

steps.title: Freeze‑dry samples to remove ethanol
steps.instruction: Transfer tubes to a freeze dryer set to an operating temperature below –80 °C and dry them; keep tubes cold at all times, then store dried tubes at –80 °C until processing. Lysis buffer may be added immediately after drying and the tubes stored at –20 °C for several months.

steps.title: Prepare additional microcentrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Label and set aside two clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes for each sample.

steps.title: Aliquot bulk beads (if used)
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.5 g of bulk beads into a sterile microcentrifuge tube for each sample; these tubes will be added to the original sample later. (Beads can also be pre‑aliquoted in the 2 mL tubes before collection or purchased as pre‑filled bead‑beating tubes.)

steps.title: Pre‑heat water baths and incubator
steps.instruction: Set a water bath to 37 °C and an incubation oven (or shaking rack) to 55 °C; set a second water bath to 65 °C and warm the 5 M NaCl stock and 10 % CTAB stock (pre‑heat to 65 °C to dissolve any CTAB crystals). If only one water bath is available, use it sequentially for the 37 °C and 65 °C steps.

steps.title: Chill centrifuge and prepare 70% ethanol
steps.instruction: Cool the centrifuge to 4 °C with a rotor that fits 2 mL tubes. Prepare fresh 70 % ethanol, chill it in an ice bucket, and keep it cold for later washes.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer and freeze‑thaw
steps.instruction: Remove dried sample tubes from –80 °C, add 570 µL lysis buffer, vortex briefly, then either snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen or return to –80 °C for at least 1 hour (overnight or longer is acceptable). This freeze‑thaw cycle aids lysis of tough cells.

steps.title: Thaw and bead‑beat (optional)
steps.instruction: Thaw tubes briefly in the pre‑heated 37 °C water bath. If beads were aliquoted, add them now and process on a Qiagen TissueLyser II (or equivalent) for 40 s at 30 Hz. Skip this step if high‑molecular‑weight DNA is required.

steps.title: Lysozyme digestion
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL Ready‑Lyse stock to each tube, mix by inversion, and incubate at 37 °C for 30 minutes with frequent mixing by inversion. Omit this step for non‑bacterial samples.

steps.title: SDS and proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL 10 % SDS stock and 3 µL proteinase K stock to each tube, mix, and incubate at 55 °C for 1 hour with frequent mixing (shaking, rotating, or manual inversion).

steps.title: Add NaCl and mix
steps.instruction: Move tubes to the 65 °C water bath, add 120 µL pre‑warmed 5 M NaCl, and mix well by inversion.

steps.title: Add CTAB and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 96 µL pre‑warmed 10 % CTAB stock, invert to mix, and incubate at 65 °C for 10 minutes with frequent inversion.

steps.title: First chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, add ~800 µL chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (or the maximum volume that fits) to each tube, vortex for 5 seconds to form an emulsion (polycarbonate filters will dissolve).

steps.title: Centrifuge first extraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 ×g, 4 °C for 5 minutes; keep tubes on ice thereafter.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, transfer the top aqueous layer (≈700 µL) to a clean 1.5 mL tube without disturbing the interphase.

steps.title: Second chloroform wash (optional)
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL chloroform:isoamyl alcohol, vortex 5 seconds, and centrifuge at 21 000 ×g, 4 °C for 5 minutes. Skip if DNA purity is not critical. Use the maximum speed available on the chilled benchtop centrifuge (older models may only reach 14 000 ×g).

steps.title: Transfer aqueous phase and record volume
steps.instruction: With a 100 µL pipette, move the top aqueous layer to a new 1.5 mL tube and record the exact volume obtained.

steps.title: Add linear polyacrylamide
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL linear polyacrylamide (LPA) solution, vortex briefly to disperse.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Calculate isopropanol volume as 0.7 × recorded aqueous volume, add that volume, and mix well by inversion.

steps.title: Incubate DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture in the dark at room temperature for at least 1 hour (preferably 2 hours). Overnight incubation at 4 °C is also acceptable.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at the maximum speed of the chilled centrifuge (ideally 21 000 ×g, 4 °C, 30 minutes; if only 14 000 ×g is reachable, extend time by ~10 minutes). Orient tubes consistently (e.g., hinges outward).

steps.title: Remove supernatant carefully
steps.instruction: Decant or pipette off the supernatant without disturbing the pellet; note that pellets may be clear, white, or faintly coloured.

steps.title: Wash pellet with cold 70% ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, rotate tubes to wash all surfaces, then centrifuge at maximum speed (≈21 000 ×g), 4 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Dry and resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Remove ethanol with a fine tip, air‑dry the pellet for 5 minutes (do not over‑dry). Resuspend in ~50 µL molecular‑grade water, TE buffer, or Tris buffer; flick the tube gently to mix. If the pellet does not dissolve, incubate at room temperature for 1 hour or in a 50 °C water bath for 10 minutes. Store the DNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality (optional)
steps.instruction: Quantify DNA with a fluorometric assay (e.g., Qubit), evaluate integrity on a 0.8–1.0 % agarose gel at low voltage (3 V/cm) using a high‑molecular‑weight marker, and measure purity ratios (A260/A280, A260/A230) with a spectrophotometer. For amplicon sequencing, use extracts directly in PCR; for whole‑genome/metagenome work, consider an additional clean‑up with a commercial kit (e.g., Zymo Genomic DNA Clean & Concentrate, Qiagen Genomic‑tips, or AMPure beads).
